newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Greek Cypriots charge Turk for spying.
newsitem.headline: Greek Cypriots charge Turk for spying.

text.p: The attorney-general's office in Cyprus on Monday charged a mainland Turk with spying on Greek Cypriot military installations and planting a bomb at a Kurdish cultural centre last year, police said.
The suspect, Najip Sari Cicekli, 45, is expected to enter a plea at a hearing of the Assizes (Criminal) court, scheduled for March 31.

Cicekli, who has lived since 1982 in the coastal town of Limassol in the Greek Cypriot-populated part of the divided island, was taken to a district court in Limassol amid draconian security measures.
He was charged with sending information on Greek and Greek Cypriot military installations and weaponry to "non-authorised persons" -- three other Turks -- between August 1994 and March 1997.
The eastern Mediterranean island has been divided since 1974, when Turkish forces invaded in the wake of a Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military ruling in Greece at the time.
A breakaway Turkish Cypriot state set up in the north of the island in 1983 is recognised only by Ankara, which has some 30,000 troops stationed there.
Cicekli also faces charges of planting a bomb at the premises of a Kurdish cultural centre in Limassol on February 10, 1996. The bomb caused substantial damage but no injuries.
Cicekli has been in custody since March 8. Two men arrested with him, a mainland Turk and a Turkish Cypriot, were released on Sunday for lack of evidence.
